title: Assistant Accountant
description:
Assistant Accountant

Location: Sheffield
Salary: Up to £35,000
12 Month Fixed Term Contract

Elevation Recruitment Group are currently working with a successful business who are looking to appoint an Assistant Accountant on a 12 month fixed term contract.

This is a varied Assistant Accountant role offering exposure across Credit Control, cash book, reconciliations, month-end and wider accounting activities. You'll take ownership of a small portfolio of high-value customers while also supporting the wider Finance team across day-to-day and month-end processes.

Key responsibilities:
- Take ownership of Credit Control for a portfolio of high-value customers, ensuring payments are received promptly and accounts are well managed.
- Manage cash book transactions and record and reconcile foreign currency transactions.
- Support the Finance team with month-end processes, journals and other accounting tasks.
- Provide cover for Purchase Ledger when required, supporting the wider team and maintaining continuity of service.
- Collect, analyse and consolidate data from a range of business systems to produce accurate and meaningful reports.
- Complete supplier and customer checks and ensure new records are set up accurately within the finance system.
- Maintain accurate financial system standing data and support the integrity of financial information.
- Work collaboratively with colleagues across Finance and the wider business to resolve queries and improve processes.

You'll need strong attention to detail, good communication skills and the ability to manage your own workload.

This is a great opportunity for a Assistant Accountant looking for a varied role with exposure across multiple areas of Finance, working within an established team on a 12 month fixed term contract.

If this Finance Assistant role looks of interest, please get in touch for more information.

title: Assistant Management Accountant
description:
Assistant Management Accountant
Sheffield, South Yorkshire

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an ambitious finance professional to join a growing business as an Assistant Management Accountant.

The role would suit either a Finance/Accounting graduate looking to start their career in management accounting, or someone with existing finance experience who is looking to take the next step, broaden their exposure and progress their career.

This is a broad, developmental role offering exposure across management accounts, financial control, commercial analysis, budgeting, forecasting, FP&A and business partnering. As you develop, you will gain increasing involvement in forecasting, budgeting, commercial analysis, and process improvement.

Key Responsibilities
- Prepare monthly management accounts, journals, and balance sheet reconciliations.
- Analyse P&L performance, investigating variances and providing commentary.
- Produce sales, margin, and management reporting.
- Assist with budgeting, forecasting, and cash flow forecasting.
- Provide financial analysis to support commercial decision-making.
- Work closely with Finance, commercial and overseas stakeholders.
- Take increasing ownership of financial analysis and business partnering as the role develops.

About You

We are open to candidates at different stages of their finance career, including graduates and those already working in finance who are ready to step up and progress.

You are likely to have:
- A relevant degree and/or previous finance experience.
- AAT qualified or studying towards CIMA, ACCA, or equivalent.
- A good understanding of accounting fundamentals.
- Strong Excel skills and confidence working with financial data.
- Excellent attention to detail and organisation.
- Good communication and relationship-building skills.
- A proactive, inquisitive approach and desire to develop.

What's on Offer
- Professional study support
- Hybrid working
- Life assurance
- Healthcare cash plan
- Exposure to management accounting, FP&A and commercial finance
- Opportunity to work closely with senior Finance and commercial stakeholders
- Clear scope for career development and increasing responsibility

title: Audience Development Coordinator - Local Authority - Libraries
description:
Audience Development Coordinator
- Hourly Rate: £15.56 PAYE
- Location: Central Sheffield
- Job Type: Hybrid (office and home working)

Join Sheffield Libraries as an Audience Development Coordinator and play a key role in bringing a vibrant programme of events and activities to life. This position offers a unique opportunity to engage with the community through a variety of events, from author talks to large-scale activities like Comic Fest and the Summer Reading Challenge.

Day-to-day of the role:
- Plan and coordinate a diverse range of events across Sheffield's libraries.
- Develop creative ideas for future events and activities.
- Support the execution of events such as author talks, history talks, re-enactments, Comic Fest, and the Summer Reading Challenge.
- Organise the upcoming Book Awards.
- Handle event administration and complete relevant forms.
- Coordinate payments for external contributors and suppliers.
- Promote library events through social media and create newsletters to showcase upcoming activities.
- Attend events to ensure smooth operation, meet and greet the public, authors, speakers, and other guests.
- Introduce authors and speakers at events as required.
- Conduct outreach and networking to develop relationships with individuals, groups, and organisations.
- Collaborate closely with colleagues and different teams across the library service.

Required Skills & Qualifications:
- Friendly, enthusiastic, and approachable demeanor.
- Creative mindset with a knack for suggesting innovative ideas.
- Highly organised with strong coordination skills.
- Confident in communicating with a diverse range of people.
- Experienced in delivering excellent customer service.
- Skilled in networking and building new relationships.
- Comfortable supporting or hosting public events.
- Proficient in using social media and creating promotional content.
- Able to balance creative initiatives with established processes and procedures.
- Capable of working both independently and as part of a team.
- Experience in events, community engagement, audience development, or related fields is advantageous.

Benefits:
- Flexible hybrid working arrangement, with approximately three office days per week.
- Opportunity to work on engaging and diverse events.
- Chance to meet a wide variety of people and make a significant impact in the community.
- Competitive hourly rate and time off in lieu (TOIL) for occasional evening or weekend work.
- Saturday overtime paid at time and a half.

How to apply:

If you're an organised, creative, and confident communicator who enjoys events and engaging with people, apply today to become part of Sheffield Libraries. Please submit your CV and a cover letter detailing your relevant experience and why you are interested in this position.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Sharp Consultancy are working with a successful business in South Sheffield who are looking to recruit an experienced Credit Controller on an initial 9 month contract.

This is a hands on role where you'll be joining a busy finance team and playing a key part in bringing down an existing aged debt backlog. The business is looking for someone who can hit the ground running, take ownership of their workload and make an immediate impact.

There is also the view of permanent employment once the initial contract has been completed and the backlog has been brought under control.

What will you be doing?

The role is varied and will cover a broad range of credit control and transactional finance duties, including:
- Managing a portfolio of customer accounts and reducing aged debt
- Chasing outstanding payments by phone and email
- Allocating cash and keeping customer accounts up to date
- Raising invoices using an ERP system
- Completing account reconciliations
- Investigating and resolving payment and account queries
- Using Excel to analyse and manage financial information
- Working closely with internal teams and customers to resolve outstanding issues
- Helping improve processes and maintain accurate financial records

What are we looking for?

We're looking for an experienced Credit Controller who is confident working in a busy environment and can get up to speed quickly.

You'll ideally have:
- Previous experience in a Credit Control role
- Experience chasing debt by both phone and email
- Good knowledge of cash allocation and account reconciliations
- Experience raising invoices
- Previous experience using an ERP or finance system
- Good Excel skills
- Strong communication and relationship-building skills
- A proactive approach and the ability to work independently
- The availability to start at short notice

This is a great opportunity for an experienced Credit Controller looking for a role where they can make a genuine impact quickly, with the potential for the position to become permanent.

If you're available immediately and this sounds like the right opportunity for you, get in touch with Sharp Consultancy today.

Sharp Consultancy is a finance and accountancy recruitment specialist assisting accounting and finance divisions of businesses in the Yorkshire and Derbyshire area. With over 30 years' experience we pride ourselves on sourcing excellent finance professionals across all divisions of an accounts function.

Candidates must be eligible to work in the UK full time without restriction. To apply please send your CV to the e-mail address stated, quoting our reference and specifying which website you saw this position advertised on. Due to the high volume of applications, we receive it is not always possible to respond to unsuccessful applicants. Therefore, if we have not responded to your application within seven days, please note that on this occasion your application has not been successful.

title: Paralegal
description:
Role: Paralegal

Location: Sheffield, South Yorkshire

Contract: Full time, permanent, hybrid

Salary: £25,000 - £27,000

As a Litigation Paralegal within this established in-house legal team, you will play a vital role in managing legal recovery claims relating to commercial property and infrastructure damage. Working within a structured, high-volume environment, your duties will include:
- Monitoring Incoming Claims: Regularly review and assess new damage claims submitted by external stakeholders, contractors, or third parties, ensuring accuracy and completeness of information.
- Case Management: Handle a personal caseload of legal recovery files from initial instruction through to final resolution. Use internal systems to track progress, maintain documentation, and ensure compliance with service level agreements.
- Claim Evaluation & Qualification: Conduct early-stage analysis of claims to determine liability, legal merit, and potential recovery value. Ensure cases meet the required thresholds for progressing to litigation where necessary.
- Negotiation & Settlement: Engage with third parties, insurers, and legal representatives to negotiate out-of-court settlements wherever possible, while protecting the organisation's commercial interests.
- Litigation Support: Where disputes cannot be resolved through negotiation, prepare case files for formal legal proceedings. This includes drafting pleadings, witness statements, and other relevant legal documents.
- Evidence Gathering: Undertake detailed investigative work by analysing technical documents, reviewing planning maps and diagrams, and liaising with internal operational teams to gather essential case facts.
- Client Liaison & Stakeholder Communication: Maintain regular contact with internal departments and external parties, including engineers, surveyors, contractors, and claims specialists, to ensure consistent information flow throughout the claims process.
- Compliance & Risk Awareness: Ensure that all casework is conducted in line with relevant legislation, regulatory standards, and internal policy. Proactively flag potential legal risks or anomalies to supervising solicitors.
- Use of Case Management Systems: Utilise specialist case management software to manage documentation, record actions, and produce reports. Contribute to data accuracy and overall operational efficiency.

title: Purchase Ledger Clerk
description:

- Updating and maintaining cash books daily.
- Bank reconciliations.
- Other ad hoc duties as required.

The Person:

- Strong organisational and time management skills are required.
